answer: Unique Embodied Presence Tokens. Each identity must anchor to a distinct physical endpoint node—a tagged jetty, falcon perch, or knoll marker—that broadcasts liveness nonces on a fixed schedule. Registration requires demonstrating continuous presence at that endpoint across randomized intervals, verified by neighboring nodes. An attacker pays the cost of deploying and maintaining separate physical hardware per identity, plus repeated in-person calibration, making mass identities geographically and operationally expensive rather than financially cheap.
